# A test firing an event through a local holding a node's handle, narrowed
# by a null test: `var b = c.b`, then `b.click()` under `if b != null`. The
# checker took a trigger only off a read of the `#id` itself, so the call
# was "no method click on type button"; it fires through the read that
# initialized the local, which is the path every target's invoker finds the
# node by.
#
# The page's only node is under an `if`, which html's prewalk then never
# met: every prop of the button fell through to setAttribute, and
# `setAttribute("disabled", false)` disabled it, so no click landed.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component page ui.node {
    var shown = true
    var clicks = 0

    if shown {
        ui.button #b(text="again", @click { clicks += 1 })
    }
}

func testAButtonUnderAnIfIsClicked(t test.Test, c page) {
    var b = c.b
    t.assert(b != null)
    if b != null {
        b.click()
    }
    t.assert(c.clicks == 1)
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
